dossier.public_summary: An 88-transit, flat-bottomed 2600 ppm dip sits on the target star with no odd/even difference or secondary eclipse and steady depth over time, consistent with a ~2.4 Earth-radius planet every 1.73 days. The orbit synchronises with the star's strong 1.73-day spot cycle, which causes large outside-of-transit brightness swings, but the transit shape and on-target centroid show the dip itself is a true transit. The planet carries over to a Gaia radius giving about a 3-Earth-radius size, needing mass and radius follow-up to confirm.

reasons.why: Difference imaging in 6 sectors puts the dip on the target and >27 sigma from any neighbour that could cause it; no plausible neighbour within 1 pixel and only 0 could_cause_within_1px, so a blended binary is ruled out.

Star density penalty 1117 is compensated by Gaia FLAME radius 0.531 vs TIC 0.431 giving duration_ratio 1.3.
